macros.name: AlsoImplementation
macros.doc: The \OnlyDescription and \AlsoImplementation declarations are intended to exclude or include the code part from the documentation.

macros.name: AtBegInputOnce
macros.doc: If you need to add something at the beginning of input of only one file, put before the respective input command an \AtBegInputOnce{〈the stuff to be added〉} declaration.

macros.name: CDPerc
macros.doc: If you declare the code delimiter other than % and then want % back, you may write \CDPerc instead of \CodeDelim⋆\%.

macros.name: changes
macros.doc: Before writing an entry to the .glo file, \changes checks if the date (the second mandatory = the third argument) is later than the date stored in the counter ChangesStartDate.

macros.name: CheckSum
macros.doc: At the beginning of the source file you may put the \CheckSum macro with a number (in one of TeX’s formats) as its argument and TeX with gmdoc shall count the number of the escape chars in the source file and tell you in the .log file (and on the terminal) whether you have typed the right number.

macros.name: CodeIndent
macros.doc: The TeX code is indented with the \CodeIndent glue and a leading space increases indentation of the line by its (space’s) width.

macros.name: CodeTopsep
macros.doc: At the points where narration begins a new line after the code or an in-line comment and where a new code line begins after the narration (that is not an in-line comment), a \CodeTopsep glue is added.

macros.name: CodeUsage
macros.doc: The \Define and \CodeUsage commands, if unstarred, mark the next scanned occurrence of their argument in the code.

macros.name: CommonEntryCmd
macros.doc: \CommonEntryCmd that stores the name of the encapsulation for the ‘common’ index entries (not special) i.e., a word that’ll become a CS that will be put before an entry in the .ind file.

macros.name: DeclareDOXHead
macros.doc: If you want to set another default family (e.g. if the code of foo.sty actually is in file bar.dtx), use \DeclareDOXHead{〈KVfamily〉}.

macros.name: Define
macros.doc: The \Define and \CodeUsage commands, if unstarred, mark the next scanned occurrence of their argument in the code.

macros.name: Describe
macros.doc: \Describe command which puts its argument in a marginpar and indexes it as a ‘usage’ entry but doesn’t print it in the text.

macros.name: DocInclude
macros.doc: \DocInclude redefines \maketitle so that it makes a chapter heading or, in the classes that don’t support \chapter, a part heading, in both cases with respective toc entries.

macros.name: FileInfo
macros.doc: The \FileInfo command takes the subsequent stuff till the closing ] and subsequent line end, extracts from it the info and writes it to the .aux and rescans the stuff.

macros.name: filenote
macros.doc: A macro for the standard note is provided, \filenote, that expands to “This file has version number 〈version number〉 dated 〈date〉.”

macros.name: GlossaryMin
macros.doc: When the glossary is started we compute the space which remains at the bottom of the current page; if this is greater than \GlossaryMin then the first part of the glossary will be placed in the available space.

macros.name: GlossaryPrologue
macros.doc: “The \GlossaryPrologue macro is used to place a short message above the glossary into the document.

macros.name: gmdmarginpar
macros.doc: To put an arbitrary text into a marginpar and have it flushed right just like the macros’ names, you are provided the \gmdmarginpar macro that takes one mandatory argument which is the contents of the marginpar.

macros.name: ilrr
macros.doc: \ilrr and \ilju commands that set \ilrrtrue and \ilrrfalse for the current in-line comment only.

macros.name: ilrrtrue
macros.doc: When you write \ilrrtrue, then all in-line comments in its scope (and their codelines) will be typeset ragged right (and still with the hanging indent).

macros.name: incs
macros.doc: \incs and \inenv commands that take analogous arguments and precede the typeset command and environment names with a % if at the beginning of a new line.

macros.name: IndexMin
macros.doc: “If multicol is in use, when the index is started we compute the remaining space on the current page; if it is greater than \IndexMin, the first part of the index will then be placed in the available space.

macros.name: IndexPrologue
macros.doc: “The \IndexPrologue macro is used to place a short message into the document above the index.

macros.name: inenv
macros.doc: \incs and \inenv commands that take analogous arguments and precede the typeset command and environment names with a % if at the beginning of a new line.

macros.name: LineNumFont
macros.doc: The line numbers (if enabled) are typeset in the \LineNumFont declaration’s scope, which is defined as {\normalfont\tiny} by default.

macros.name: ltxLookSetup
macros.doc: If you prefer more ltxdocish look, in which the files always constitute the parts and those parts have a part’s title pages with the file name and the files’ \maketitles result in (article-like) titles not division headings, then you are provided the \ltxLookSetup declaration (allowed only in the preamble).

macros.name: opt
macros.doc: For an optional arguments use \opt which wraps the item label in square brackets.

macros.name: qemph
macros.doc: An emphasis command for ‘queer’ line ends.

macros.name: ResumeAllDefining
macros.doc: \ResumeAllDefining discards the effect of any \DeclareDefining that could have occurred between \HideAllDefining and itself.

macros.name: ResumeDefining
macros.doc: The \ResumeDefining command takes a defining command as the argument and resumes its automatic detection.

macros.name: stanzaskip
macros.doc: The \stanzaskip’s value is assigned also to the display skips and to \topsep.

macros.name: TextUsage
macros.doc: The \TextUsage (one-argument) command is intended to mark usage of a verbatim occurrence of a TeX object in the commentary.

envs.name: enumargs
envs.doc: enumargs environment which is a version of enumerate with labels like #.
